A.why: Best front bell skirt and a rope belt, but the teal bodice and shoulders dominate from above and the back reads as a coat.
A.fix: Cut teal to the sash and trim only; recolour the bodice and shoulders driftwood or sand, and carry the bell flare round the back.

B.why: Slate column with saturated blue shoulder slabs: it reads as a military greatcoat with no waist or flare, off-palette.
B.fix: Drop the cobalt shoulder tops, move to the driftwood/salt palette, then cinch the waist and flare the hem.

C.why: Well-muted salt palette and a laced sailcloth front, but a straight narrow skirt with bulky cuffs reads close to the linen robe.
C.fix: Belt the waist and flare the skirt to the shins; slim the cuffed sleeves and raise the headpiece.

D.why: The tiered salt skirt is the strongest, most distinct gown silhouette from ARPG, with an on-brief palette and a driftwood quill crest, but the hard flat tiers read as a cake or plinth and the torso is boxy.
D.fix: Turn the stepped tiers into sloped, overlapping flounces ending at the shins; narrow the shoulders and sleeves to make a waist.

E.why: Best palette (sand, driftwood, sparse teal), clearest corseted waist and a smooth A-line, but the headpiece vanishes from above and the sleeves are wide.
E.fix: Add a tall shell/coral/driftwood headpiece; slim the stacked sleeves and push the hem flare one step wider.

F.why: The corsair tricorn is the best theme read, but the waist shelf, boxy straight skirt, cobalt shoulder caps and trouser-like dark back stop it reading as a dress.
F.fix: Remove the hip ledge and flare the skirt as one continuous panel front and back; recolour the shoulder caps.

notes: No set is fully there. D owns the silhouette, E owns the palette and waist, and F owns the theme (tricorn). The ideal would be D's flare, softened into flounces, on E's colours, with a corsair or shell headpiece. Common faults: wide box shoulders and stacked sleeves across most sets (against the narrow-shoulder brief), dark plain backs that stop reading as a gown, and off-palette cobalt on B and F. Teal is overused only on A.
